And what I saw was that American movies try to play it safe, American horror movies. They don't want to offend people. And so the kind of directors like Miike understand that what makes a great horror movie is that it lives in that danger zone, that dangerous territory. And it harkens back to kind of Italian cinema in the 70s, films like Cannibal Holocaust or Pasolini's Salo, where they're making movies that are so violent, but they're not trying to please everybody. They're not for everybody. They're for a very specific audience. They're like, this is a sick movie. If you don't like it, stay the hell away from it. And I just felt like nobody was doing anything like that in America. So that's what I wanted to do. And I also like the fact that the Asian films aren't really pure. They're not really pure.
